claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has an approximately 786 MPa quasi-static yield strength.
The starting alloy has an approximately 1314 MPa quasi-static compressive strength.
The starting alloy has an approximately 13.5% quasi-static fracture strain.
A minor Nb addition combined with tailored heat treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale precipitates in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Precipitate-mediated dislocation pinning will enhance dynamic strain hardening.
Enhanced dynamic strain hardening will delay shear-band propagation and strain localization.
Delayed localization will improve uniform plastic deformation.
Delayed localization will reduce the rate of abrupt impact-induced energy release.
The Nb-modified, heat-treated alloy will have approximately 10–20% higher dynamic yield strength than the baseline.
The Nb-modified, heat-treated alloy will have approximately 10–20% higher dynamic compressive strength than the baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will exhibit a fracture strain greater than 13.5% under adiabatic dynamic loading.
The Nb-modified alloy will exhibit more controlled and reduced impact-induced energy release than the baseline.
The unmodified alloy has limited strain hardening and poor uniform deformability under high-strain-rate adiabatic loading.
The unmodified alloy fails rapidly under high-strain-rate adiabatic loading.
The predicted benefits apply at strain rates above 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic dynamic loading.
A Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar can impose the specified high-strain-rate dynamic deformation.
